claim: For any Borel probability measure \(\rho\) on \((0,\tfrac12)\), let \(V\sim\rho\) and let \(Z,\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2,\ldots\) be mutually independent standard normal variables, independent of \(V\), and set \(X_i=\frac{\sqrt{1-2V}}{2}Z+\sqrt V\,\varepsilon_i\). Then \((X_i)_{i\ge1}\) is infinitely exchangeable and \(X_i+X_j\sim N(0,1)\) for every \(i\ne j\), regardless of \(\rho\); its covariance matrix depends on \(\rho\) only through \(\mathbb EV\), while the characteristic function of \(X_i-X_j\) is \(\int e^{-vt^2}\rho(dv)\), which uniquely identifies \(\rho\). If \(\rho\) is nondegenerate, the process is not Gaussian because its marginal fourth cumulant is \(3\operatorname{Var}(V)/4>0\). In particular, \(\rho_1=\delta_{1/4}\) and \(\rho_2=\tfrac12\delta_{1/8}+\tfrac12\delta_{3/8}\) yield the same Gaussian pair-sum law and identical covariance matrices, but respectively a Gaussian and a non-Gaussian exchangeable process.

correctness.rationale: Conditional on \((V,Z)\), the sequence is iid Gaussian, hence infinitely exchangeable. Conditional on \(V\), each pair sum is \(N(0,1)\) because the independent variances add to \(1-2V+2V=1\). The marginal variance is \(\frac14+\frac12\mathbb EV\) and pair covariance is \(\frac14-\frac12\mathbb EV\). The fourth cumulant equals \(3\operatorname{Var}(V)/4\), so it is positive for nondegenerate \(\rho\). The pair-difference characteristic function is the Laplace transform of \(\rho\), which uniquely determines a finite measure on \([0,1/2]\). The explicit rational example is checked by the included standard-library script.

originality.rationale: The general failure of exchangeable-sequence identification from partial sums is prior literature, and the joint-pair Gaussian rigidity theorem is also prior. The originality claim is limited to the explicit all-\(\rho\) Gaussian pair-sum family, the covariance-matched Gaussian/non-Gaussian pair, and exact recovery of \(\rho\) from pair differences. Targeted semantic and literature searches found no direct equivalent; a differently phrased Gaussian random-effects construction remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: A similar conditional-Gaussian random-effects construction may exist under different terminology outside the inspected sources.

The construction does not address whether Gaussian one-dimensional marginals plus a Gaussian pair sum could imply additional rigidity.

value.rationale: The family supplies an exact, all-parameter boundary for a natural Gaussianity diagnostic: Gaussianity of each pair sum and the complete second-order covariance structure do not identify whether an infinite exchangeable process is Gaussian. The two explicit laws with equal mean mixing parameter exhibit the failure exactly, with fourth-cumulant gap 3/256. Pair differences provide a natural identifying observable within the family through a unique Laplace transform. This is a reusable structural counterexample rather than a simulation-only result.
